name: Gastr del Sol
label: Drag City
lede: A Louisville punk turned Chicago grad student, named his new band half after his old one and half after a Derby winner, then spent five years taking rock songs apart with Jim O'Rourke until the two of them stopped talking.

eras.title: From Squirrel Bait to Bastro
eras.text: David Grubbs came up in Louisville's teenage punk scene, then moved his loud power trio to Chicago for graduate school. By 1991 he was tired of the same sound every night, and Gastr del Sol was how he got out.

years.h: Squirrel Bait forms in Louisville on Halloween
years.p: [[Squirrel Bait|5dbf117b-c076-4d3b-b7ae-13517c25b2cf]], first called Squirrelbait Youth, starts with [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] on guitar. The band's guitarist Brian McMahan later forms [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]].

years.h: David Grubbs starts Bastro after Squirrel Bait ends
years.p: [[Bastro|cfc5b1bf-a46c-4504-bcb6-a820416a1894]] is a post-hardcore power trio: Grubbs, ex-Squirrel Bait bassist Clark Johnson, and later drummer [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] from My Dad Is Dead. Three albums follow on Homestead Records.

years.h: Clark Johnson leaves for law school; Bundy K. Brown steps in
years.p: Bassist Clark Johnson quits Bastro for law school. [[Bundy K. Brown|940101f1-79c7-40ac-98d3-7b924b244a8e]] joins [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] and [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]], and the last Bastro shows already sketch Gastr del Sol songs.
years.xp:
Grubbs told Paris Transatlantic that Bastro was always the same sound, the same group, the same instrumentation, and they needed to change how they worked. He went back to piano and acoustic guitar.

Live tapes from those final Bastro shows came out in 2005 as Antlers: Live 1991 on Grubbs's Blue Chopsticks label.

eras.title: Half a band name, half a racehorse
eras.text: The trio rearranged Bastro's instrumentals for acoustic instruments and gave the result a name that sounded like a foreign word and wasn't. Then Tortoise pulled Brown and McEntire away, and a young Chicago guitarist asked his way in.

years.h: Gastr del Sol is named after Bastro and a Derby winner
years.p: [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] blended Bastro with Gato del Sol, the horse that won the 1982 Kentucky Derby.

years.h: The Serpentine Similar, Gastr del Sol's debut, on TeenBeat
years.p: Recorded September to November 1992 in Chicago and Minneapolis with [[Brian Paulson|65f13d3b-ddd6-4b33-8ab7-366ee7fb63c4]]. All eight songs are by [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] and [[Bundy K. Brown|940101f1-79c7-40ac-98d3-7b924b244a8e]].
years.xp: It came out on TeenBeat Records, the D.C.-area label run by [[Unrest|f444dc7d-59c1-4ed6-beb7-f90b6d85366c]]'s Mark Robinson. Drag City reissued it on June 16, 1997.

years.h: Bundy K. Brown and John McEntire drift off to Tortoise
years.p: [[Bundy K. Brown|940101f1-79c7-40ac-98d3-7b924b244a8e]] and [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] put their time into [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]]. McEntire keeps playing on Gastr records and tours with them.

years.h: Jim O'Rourke joins after hearing The Serpentine Similar
years.p: [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] first wanted a heavy guitar band and the early rehearsals flopped. After he heard the finished debut, he asked in. By October he's recording Crookt, Crackt, or Fly.

eras.title: Jim and David
eras.text: For four years Gastr del Sol was two people, David Grubbs and Jim O'Rourke, with John McEntire on the road. They made acoustic guitar records that fell apart on purpose, a chamber piece, and records with Tony Conrad, and helped give Chicago's post-rock its reputation.

years.h: Crookt, Crackt, or Fly, and the song that named The Sea and Cake
years.p: Gastr del Sol's first Drag City album, engineered by [[Brian Paulson|65f13d3b-ddd6-4b33-8ab7-366ee7fb63c4]]. [[Sam Prekop|33175dbe-db6c-4f0b-a4c6-9addcd403186]]'s band [[The Sea and Cake|74171cb6-1ff8-42bd-be8a-96660c22e3e0]] got its name from mishearing the song title "The C in Cake".
years.xp: Two of its eight tracks, "Work from Smoke" and "The Wrong Soundings", run more than twelve minutes each. [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]], Steve Butters and Gene Coleman on bass clarinet sit in.

years.p: A short follow-up to Crookt, Crackt, or Fly.

years.h: David Grubbs plays guitar on Codeine's The White Birch
years.p: [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] adds guitar to two songs on [[Codeine|cecd5f91-cfdd-45d1-879f-3920c7c76e58]]'s second album, on Sub Pop.

years.h: The Harp Factory on Lake Street: one 17-minute chamber piece
years.p: A single composition for chamber orchestra, produced by [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] for Table of the Elements. The title is the Lyon & Healy harp factory at Lake and Ogden in Chicago.

years.h: Gastr del Sol record with Tony Conrad and cover an AIDS benefit
years.p: They make The Japanese Room at La Pagode with violinist [[Tony Conrad|39b56aa8-5d36-49ab-ae5e-c3aa836b6620]], and give "Quietly Approaching" to the Red Hot benefit Red Hot + Bothered.

years.h: Upgrade & Afterlife ends on a John Fahey song with Tony Conrad
years.p: The closer is a [[John Fahey|95bb27d2-43c7-4a92-85ee-f95a245f0ee4]] cover with [[Tony Conrad|39b56aa8-5d36-49ab-ae5e-c3aa836b6620]] on violin. The opener's title is a cheap public-restroom perfume.
years.xp:
David Grubbs said Conrad got involved after a Gastr show in Atlanta, where he saw Conrad literally dancing as [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] played the Fahey tune alone. The cover photo is Swiss artist Roman Signer's Wasserstiefel, water boots.

Reviews split hard: Alternative Press gave it five out of five, the NME four out of ten.

eras.title: Chamber pop, then silence
eras.text: Gastr del Sol's last album was its most tuneful, strings and horns and even a guest vocal. By the summer after it came out, David Grubbs and Jim O'Rourke weren't working together any more.

years.p: [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]], [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] and Oval's Markus Popp wrote it. [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] drums and engineers, with [[Rob Mazurek|73c34525-f9c6-4c33-9abe-007748aaebe5]], [[Ken Vandermark|e5a4107f-5bb3-4f24-b9b7-927bb23840b5]] and singer [[Edith Frost|289faaeb-96bf-41ff-a15f-5166b6298e01]] as guests.
years.xp: Pitchfork put it at number 38 on its list of 1998's best albums. Fact later placed it tenth among the greatest post-rock records.

q: Jim, as the strong personality, kind of crowds people out of bands.
years.h: David Grubbs declares Gastr del Sol finished
years.p: By June 1998 David Grubbs had stopped working with Jim O'Rourke. Wikipedia puts the split down to personal differences and grievances.
years.xp:
Grubbs told Paris Transatlantic that O'Rourke, the strong personality, tended to crowd people out of bands. The two also shut down Dexter's Cigar, their reissue imprint on Drag City, to make a clean break.

O'Rourke joined [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] the next year and went on to produce [[Wilco|9e53f84d-ef44-4c16-9677-5fd4d78cbd7d]]; Grubbs kept making records for Drag City and became a professor at Brooklyn College.

eras.title: Opening the archive
eras.text: Gastr del Sol never reunited on record, but the vaults opened: first the Bastro tapes that started it, then a Gastr box nearly a quarter-century after the split.

years.h: Antlers: Live 1991 finally issues Bastro's last shows
years.p: [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]]'s Blue Chopsticks label releases the 1991 Bastro recordings where the first Gastr del Sol songs took shape.

years.h: We Have Dozens of Titles: the Gastr del Sol archive on Drag City
years.p: A 3LP box of uncollected studio recordings and unreleased live sets, released nearly 25 years after the band broke up.
